method: Synthetic JSON payload, 32 archive records, 8 jobs, 2 Tokio request workers, 10ms heartbeat. The same Audit::record implementation was compared on request workers and spawn_blocking workers. Mode order alternated. Temp directories only; no credentials, upstream or production archive.
conclusion: Synchronous archive I/O can starve request workers for seconds. Offloading removes the scheduler stall in this controlled workload, while total write duration remains similar. Buffering reduces write-call amplification.
limitations: Not a measurement of production disconnect causation or frequency.
Production binary has no function symbols, limiting attribution of sampled live stacks.

A production writer needs bounded count/byte queues, observable overflow and write failures, ordered shutdown and explicit durability behavior. Naively spawning a blocking task per event creates an unbounded backlog.
